items.fix: Follow-up: make the 404 SSR response render the component's not-found markup (for example NavigationManager.NotFound() with a NotFound page, or status-code re-execution) instead of an empty body.

subject: implementer
reason: The fix stops non-positive ids from reaching Catalog.API, which answered 400 and caused the 500. It sends them through the same SetNotFound() path as a Catalog 404, so /item/0 and /item/-1 return the same 404 page as /item/999999. Behaviour for existing products is unchanged, and the change stays inside the WebApp page without a broad catch or any API contract change.

items.reason: The non-positive-id check returns before isLoggedIn is set. It is harmless today because the not-found page does not use it, but it could surprise someone who later adds login-dependent markup to the not-found page.
items.fix: No change needed now. If login-dependent markup is ever added to the not-found branch, set isLoggedIn before the check.

items.title: Unknown product id 999999 answers 404 with the Not found page
items.reason: The story defines the expected answer for 0 and -1 as "exactly as `/item/999999` does", so the reference page itself must be pinned: if it changed, cases 02 and 03 would be checking against a moving target. It needs the e2e layer because the status and page come from the WebApp rendering on the test stack, with Catalog.API answering 404 for the unknown id.

items.title: Product id 0 answers 404 with the same Not found page
covers: Expected: /item/0 answers 404 and the same page as /item/999999
items.reason: This is the reported defect: `/item/0` answered `500` because Catalog.API answers 400 for it and the page did not handle that. 0 is the boundary just below the first catalog id (1), so it is a separate case from the negative id. The e2e layer is required because the acceptance criterion is the status and page the running WebApp serves.

items.title: Product id -1 answers 404 with the same Not found page
covers: Expected: /item/-1 answers 404 and the same page as /item/999999
items.reason: The story names `/item/-1` as a second failing input: a negative id is a different class of invalid input from 0, and a fix that only special-cased 0 would still answer `500` here. The e2e layer is required because the acceptance criterion is the status and page the running WebApp serves.

items.title: Existing product id 1 still answers 200 with its product page
covers: Expected: product pages of existing products behave as they do today
items.reason: The fix adds a guard on the id (`ItemId <= 0` is not found); an off-by-one (`< 1` written as `<= 1`) would turn the first real product into a 404. Id 1 is the boundary just inside the valid range and an existing seeded product, so it checks both the boundary and the story's "existing products behave as they do today". The e2e layer matches the other cases: the status and page come from the running WebApp.

subject: implementer
reason: The item page answers 404 for 999999, 0 and -1, but the body is empty, so the Not found page the plan requires is never shown.

items.expected: GET /item/999999 answers 404 and shows h1 'Not found', '.item-page .item-notfound' 'Sorry, we couldn't find any such product.' and a visible 'Back to catalog' link
items.actual: 404 with Content-Length: 0; the browser shows a blank white page; '.eshop-hero-intro h1' is not found
items.reason: The page has markup for its not-found state, but setting the 404 status while rendering on .NET 10 makes the server end the response with an empty body, so that markup is never sent

items.expected: GET /item/0 answers 404 with the same Not found page (title, message, Back to catalog link)
items.reason: Same cause: the new guard goes through SetNotFound(), which produces an empty 404 body, not the Not found page
